_: WHAT A MERCHANT'S HULL CARRIES — docs/SHIPS_AND_GEAR.md §3.2 (S2, migration 0126). Endowed at founding, as her hull is; never bought, never changed (owner, 2026-10-15: merchant gear is FIXED).
_how: public.npc_fit_loadout(ship) picks ONE pattern of her class, deterministically per FLEET — md5(fleet_id) mod the class's pattern count — so every hull of a fleet wears the same pattern and a re-run picks the same one. Each item goes on through public.mount_fitting, the same core a player's FIT uses, so a pattern that does not fit her slots is refused, not squeezed.
_hold: No pattern spends hold (owner, 2026-10-15: prefer loadouts that do not reduce hold). So no anchor, no rudder, no broadside guns, no powder magazine: each of those costs tuns. The only hold change is the nau trader's hold fittings, +25 t.
_never_full: A pattern never fills every slot: a full hull is the player's design, not the world's default.
_s18: 0167 (S18): a merchant of a line with its own hull for her class sails that hull (public.npc_line_hulls, scripts/build-ships.mjs `merchant`) and wears THESE patterns of the live class it stands in for — public.npc_fit_loadout reads them through npc_line_hulls, so no pattern is written twice.
_guard: migration 0126 seeds public.npc_loadouts with exactly these rows; S7 adds this file to scripts/db/world-guard.mjs.
_far_traders: 0404 (S4, docs/SEA_CONDITIONS_AND_REGIONS.md): the six far-trader hulls (taforeia, retour, nao, hourque of size 4; indiaman, naucarr of size 5) wear ONE pattern: deal planking and a sheet anchor, wave +6, so a size-4 hull reads 57 and holds every sea but the open Pacific. This pattern does spend hold (the sheet anchor), against `_hold`: holding the ocean is what these houses are for.
